newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban said advancing in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said advancing in northwest.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia captured a key district in the northwestern province of Faryab on Wednesday after heavy fighting with opposition forces, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said Taleban fighters had taken the Qaysar district after seizing Ghormach town in neighbouring Badghis province and were advancing towards the Faryab capital Maimana, about 60 km (38 miles) to the northeast.
No independent confirmation was immediately available about the gains of Taleban, which control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, including the capital Kabul.

AIP quoted its sources in the area as saying that 21 soldiers of northern opposition militia commander General Abdul Malik were killed and 75 arrested in the offensive launched by a 1,500-strong Taleban force on Wednesday morning.
At least six Taleban were also killed, it said.
